correctness.rationale: For every odd clique coordinate the all-ones operator is rank-one idempotent, splitting the tensor into parity eigenspaces of integer dimensions (U±Delta)/2. Every even coordinate has a rank-one square-zero block and m_i−2 trivial blocks; an explicit contracting homotopy computes tensor-sum homology H and rank (V−H)/2. Combining the two pieces proves exact Jordan blocks at eigenvalues 0 and 1. The decomposition immediately proves the nested-kernel entry counts and the fixed and primitive-two-cycle counts over every q=2^f. A standalone direct adjacency-matrix and state-enumeration verifier passed 341 rank cases and 335,564 exact configurations in 17 finite cases. Finite tests corroborate rather than replace the proof. Both b0 and b1 are positive for each genuinely mixed graph.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The closest published matrix methods cover a stronger-looking ambient category of graphs only in a different sense: Peeters explicitly imposes the distance-regular uniform alphabet, while the present heterogeneous Cartesian graph usually is not distance regular. Classical semisimple real spectra cannot imply nilpotent Jordan chain sizes in characteristic two. A general tensor-product textbook lemma might make the proof elementary, but no located cited result subsumes the precise dynamical census.

originality.rationale: Claim restricted to mixed odd/even coordinate sizes. Peeters (2002), Section 3, Theorems 3.1 and 3.4, gives modular ranks for uniform Hamming graphs and precedes the tensor method; his stated results do not determine mixed-product zero/one Jordan multiplicities or transient and periodic-state populations. Tadaki (1993) treats 1D path automata; Rowland–Yassawi treats bi-infinite linear automata with memory; graph-square real spectral work addresses a different operator. Actual semantic searches of published research records and targeted primary-literature searches did not locate an equivalent all-mixed-parity theorem. This is qualified by possible unindexed earlier work and the elementary method.
residual_risks: Peeters (2002) gives closely related modular-rank tensor methods; an algebraically equivalent heterogeneous generalization might exist as an unpublished exercise or in an unindexed source.
A 2023 generalized-Hamming graph paper could not be examined fully; accessible statements indicate spectral graph squares, but cannot exclude an unexpected appendix.
No finite collection of scholarly searches proves worldwide historical novelty.

value.rationale: Products of complete graphs model finite heterogeneous Hamming alphabets. Mixing an even and odd coordinate changes dynamics qualitatively: primitive two-cycle oscillation and genuine two-step relaxation coexist for every such product. The exact complete infinite-family Jordan decomposition, transient populations and cycle counts provide meaningful structural and quantitative invariants not given by purely uniform-alphabet modular ranks or real spectra. The claim is not merely a computational microcase.
